chunks: What he narrated from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his uncle Yaʿqūb al-Aḥmar, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a woman who had been menstruating and then saw purity: may her husband have intercourse with her before she performs ghusl (ritual bath)? He said: “No, not until she performs ghusl (ritual bath).”

He said: And I asked him about a woman who menstruated while traveling, then became pure, but did not find water for a day or two. Is it lawful for her husband to have intercourse with her before she performs ghusl (ritual bath)? He said: “It is not proper until she performs ghusl (ritual bath).”

key_terms.الطُّهْرَ: cessation of menstruation and return to purity
key_terms.لَا يَصْلُحُ: it is not proper or acceptable

ai.seo_question: Can a husband have intercourse with his wife after her menstruation ends but before she performs ghusl (ritual bath)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a menstruating woman who has become pure. It states that her husband may not have intercourse with her until she has performed ghusl (ritual bath), even if she is traveling and unable to find water for one or two days.
